evidence: "The required rate against the ~1.08 s two-term prefill residual (TTFT SLO minus retrieval time — an upper cap, not a deployable prefill target; see Ch 4, Table 4-2)"
issue: Ch 2 §2.3 refers to the 1.2 s value as 'TTFT SLO', but Ch 4 §4.3 explicitly states 'The 1.2 s and ~25 ms values are design budgets, not the pass/fail SLO thresholds. Pass/fail on a measured distribution is judged against the p95 ceilings (TTFT ≤ 2 s, TPOT ≤ 35 ms)'. The book holds this distinction sharply elsewhere (e.g. Ch 4 Table 4-1 'Latency' row: 'TTFT budget 1.2 s … p95 ceiling ≤ 2 s'); Ch 2 §2.3 is the one place that calls 1.2 s an SLO. The terminology slip directly contradicts the canonical Latency dimension definition.
fix_instruction: Change 'TTFT SLO' to 'TTFT budget' on page 30 to match Ch 4's explicit design-budget-vs-SLO distinction.

evidence: "the head glyphs schematic: the canonical model has 64 query and 64 KV heads per layer (Ch. 4, Table 4-2), so the four drawn heads stand for the enumeration, not the model's head count. The token labels mark sequence positions, not the sampled-versus-input distinction"
issue: The caption first says the four drawn heads 'stand for the enumeration, not the model's head count' (i.e. a schematic abbreviation), then immediately says 'the token labels mark sequence positions, not the sampled-versus-input distinction, so the one-step write offset described above is stated in this caption rather than drawn.' The caption simultaneously tells the reader the drawing is schematic (heads, tokens) AND that it accurately represents sequence positions — two contradictory readings of what the figure encodes. A reader cannot tell whether token₁/token₂/token₃ labels are a faithful representation of sequence positions or another schematic abbreviation.
fix_instruction: Make the schematic-scope statement uniform across the caption: either state that token labels are also schematic (like the head glyphs), or rephrase to distinguish explicitly which elements are faithful (positions) and which are abbreviated (head count).

evidence: "(All figures trace to the canonical scenario (Ch. 4, Table 4-2); none are measurement claims.)"
issue: The table header calls every row '(worked example, not reference)' and says 'none are measurement claims,' but the first two rows ('input tokens / request ~9,200' and 'output tokens / request ~300') carry no [DERIVED] label — they are the [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] inputs. The remaining rows are [DERIVED]. Calling an assumed input a 'worked example' conflates input with computation: an assumption is the scenario setup, not a worked result. The header's blanket classification hides the Assumption/Derived split that the book's own evidence discipline (Preface, §2-axis note) requires.
fix_instruction: Either add the [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] labels to the first two rows and [canonical scenario][DERIVED] to the computed rows (matching Table 1-1's derivation column pattern), or change the header to '(assumed inputs and derived results of the canonical scenario)' rather than '(worked example, not reference)'.
